payroll_function.title: Payroll 1 — The Payroll Function & Salary Structures
payroll_function.desc: The foundation of the payroll certification: payroll as the organ between HR and finance, the three numbers and pay-as-structure philosophy, salary components with their statutory flags, the salary structure per grade, effective-dated assignments, the gross-to-net walk with the modeling discipline, and the governance of the pay masters.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — Payroll: the organ between
lessons.html:
Welcome to the sixth certification — and the one two tracks deliberately deferred. The HR track drew its boundary in its first chapter (HR owns the inputs payroll consumes); the Accounts track carried only payroll's journal and its tax custody. This track is the organ BETWEEN: payroll — the function that consumes the people facts, computes the pay, holds the state's money in passing, and writes the largest recurring entry in most trading firms' books.

The two boundaries, now seen from inside. Payroll's position defines its discipline: UPSTREAM, it receives the HR track's packages (the attendance close's days and categories, the leave interface's treatments, the movement notifications with effective dates, the joiner and separation packages — module by module, the HR track built payroll's supplier network, and this track is the customer whose specifications those handoffs met); DOWNSTREAM, it delivers to finance (the payroll journal into the ledger — Accounts 2's lawful catalogue receiving its biggest monthly resident; the statutory custody accounts — Accounts 5's machinery receiving PAYE and pension in passing; the bank payment run — Accounts 3's separations governing the money's actual movement) and to the WORKFORCE (the salaries themselves, and the payslips that account for them — module 4). A function with this many counterparties runs on interfaces or it runs on apologies — the HR track's closing law (interfaces over blur), now taught from the middle of the sandwich.

The precision stakes. Why payroll's error tolerance is the firm's lowest, taught before any machinery: a stock error costs money; a salary error costs money AND trust, at a ratio no other function faces — the underpaid worker's family felt the shortfall at the market before the correction posted (the error is personal, immediate, and remembered), the overpaid worker's clawback is a grievance regardless of the error's honesty, and the workforce recalibrates its trust in EVERY firm system by whether the pay lands right (the firm whose payroll is exact earns patience for every other imperfection; the one whose payroll wobbles is distrusted on things it does perfectly). Add the state's stakes — the statutory deductions held in custody (module 2), where error compounds into penalty — and the function's character emerges: payroll is the discipline where 'approximately right' does not exist, which is why this track's laws will be the academy's strictest.

The trilogy completed. The scope, stated: this track covers the salary structures (this module), the Nigerian statutory layer at full depth (module 2 — the track's ten-chapter deep module, sibling to the tax module it extends), the run itself (module 3), the payslip and its confidentiality (module 4), variable pay (module 5), the review machinery (module 6), exits and special cases (module 7), and the structural layer (module 8). What stays at the boundaries it honours: the PEOPLE decisions (who is hired, promoted, disciplined — the HR track's terrain, consumed here as effective-dated facts), the LEDGER's wider life (the accounts beyond payroll's entries — the Accounts track's terrain, fed here), and the tax POSITIONS where law is unclear (the adviser's terrain, in the settled grammar of both prior tracks). The consultant completing this track holds all three organs — the people, the pay, and the books — and the joins between them, which is the full anatomy of how a Nigerian trading firm keeps its people paid, legal, and accounted.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Pay in structure: the vocabulary & the philosophy
lessons.html:
Before components and formulas, the vocabulary that every offer conversation, statutory computation, and payslip dispute turns on — and the design philosophy that makes pay a STRUCTURE rather than a pile of negotiations. The foundations chapter.

The three numbers. Every compensation conversation involves three figures that Nigerian practice constantly conflates, and the consultant untangles them on day one: GROSS — the earnings before deductions (the sum of the salary components — the number the structure defines and module 2's computations mostly reference); NET — what lands in the account (gross minus the employee's deductions: the statutory shares, the governed recoveries — the number the WORKER means when they say 'my salary', which is why Chapter 6's net-preview discipline exists: the offer stated in gross to a candidate thinking in net is the misunderstanding that sours week four's payday); and the EMPLOYER'S TOTAL COST — gross plus the employer's own statutory contributions (the pension employer share, the levies of module 2 — the number the OWNER should budget with, and rarely does until shown: the ₦250k gross hire costs meaningfully more than ₦250k, and the budget that ignores the employer layer discovers it in module 2's remittance season). Three numbers, three audiences, one structure computing all of them — the vocabulary is the first deliverable.

Pay as structure: the design philosophy. The thesis this module builds toward its law: compensation in a governed firm is COMPUTED from structure — the component definitions (Chapter 3), the salary structures per grade (Chapter 4), the person's assignment (Chapter 5) — not NEGOTIATED from memory (the per-person arrangement recalled by the founder, adjusted by mood, discovered at dispute). The structure's dividends, enumerated: CONSISTENCY (same grade, same structure — the pay-disparity time bomb of HR 2's offer chapter, defused at its source), COMPUTABILITY (the statutory layer computes from component definitions — module 2 is only possible because Chapter 3's flags exist), EXPLAINABILITY (every payslip line traceable to a structure line — module 4's query-killing transparency), and CHANGEABILITY (the review that moves a band moves everyone on it — module 6's machinery, impossible against 27 private arrangements). The philosophy's honest cost, stated too: structure constrains improvisation — which is the point, and the owner who wants to 'just add something for Tunde this month' will meet Chapter 7's governance and module 5's channels, because the something-for-Tunde that bypasses structure is the favour disease (the HR track's oldest villain) wearing a bank transfer.

The component conventions. The Nigerian structural reality previewed for Chapter 3: pay here is conventionally STRUCTURED into named components — basic, housing, transport, and the allowances beyond — a convention with teeth, because statutory computations and common practice reference the components (the pension contribution's base is conventionally basic-plus-housing-plus-transport; benefit conventions and some computations key off basic) — so component design is not cosmetic labelling: the SPLIT chosen (what share of gross sits in basic) has downstream consequences the accountant and adviser weigh, and the consultant's job is the machinery that makes whatever split the professionals choose compute correctly, evenly, forever. The chapter closes where the module's law will: the structure is the single source of pay truth — everything else in this track is machinery for defining it, computing from it, governing it, and explaining it.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Salary components: the anatomy
lessons.html:
The atoms of pay: the SALARY COMPONENTS — defined once, flagged precisely, reused everywhere. The component chapter, where module 2's computability is won or lost.

Earnings components. The additions, defined as masters: basic (the anchor component — the conventions that reference it make its share a design decision, not a default), housing and transport (the classic Nigerian trio completed — together with basic forming the conventional base for the pension computation module 2 details), the further allowances the firm's structure uses (meal, utility, and the like — named per the firm's policy, resisted per the sprawl warning below), and the VARIABLE earnings that module 5 governs (overtime, bonus, commission — defined here as components with their flags, populated there by their documents). Each earnings component carries its flags: taxability (feeding module 2's PAYE base), statutory-base membership (in or out of the pension base — the flag the computation reads), and the formula-versus-amount nature below.

Deduction components. The subtractions, in their two families: the STATUTORY deductions (employee PAYE, the employee pension share, NHF where applicable — module 2's whole terrain, defined here as components whose formulas the statutory chapter will fill), and the GOVERNED recoveries (the loan repayment, the salary-advance recovery, the documented deduction of HR 7's separation package — each a component that posts only from its authorising document, never from a typed number: module 5 holds their governance, and the improvised-deduction conviction of two prior tracks holds here hardest of all, because THIS is the layer where improvised deductions actually execute).

Formula versus amount. The component's computational nature: AMOUNT components (the fixed figure the structure states — basic as a stated sum), FORMULA components (computed from others — housing as a percentage of basic, the pension share as its statutory rate on its statutory base, PAYE as module 2's full computation), and the design discipline that keeps structures maintainable: formulas reference NAMED bases (the pension formula reads the flagged base, not a hardcoded sum of three components — so the structure that adds a component to the base changes one flag, not five formulas), the precedence is explicit (components computing from components compute in order — the circular formula is the structure that cannot run), and the formulas live in the STRUCTURE layer, not scattered per person (Chapter 4's whole argument).

Component governance: the sprawl warning. The master-data laws, sixth appearance, with this layer's specific disease named: COMPONENT SPRAWL — the allowance invented per negotiation ('special duty allowance' for one hire, 'transition allowance' for another) until the component list is a museum of old deals, every statutory flag a per-component audit, and every payslip a glossary. The fixes are the familiar ones: components created by the narrowest pen (Chapter 7), named from a governed list, justified by policy (a component exists because a CLASS of pay exists, not because a negotiation happened — the one-off lands in module 5's additional-pay machinery with its document, not in the component list), flagged at creation with the accountant's confirmation (the taxability flag set wrong on day one mis-computes every person, every month, until found — the component review is module 2's pre-season ritual for exactly this reason), and audited annually beside the structures (the component nobody's structure uses is retired, not kept 'just in case'). The chapter's one-liner for the implementation file: few components, precisely flagged, formula-driven — the payroll that is easy to explain is the payroll that was designed this way.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The salary structure: the master
lessons.html:
The components assemble into the layer's central master: the SALARY STRUCTURE — the named template of components and formulas that defines what a class of employees earns. The structure chapter.

The structure as template. One structure per pay CLASS — in a graded firm, per grade (HR 1's band architecture receiving its payroll payload: the grade that carried leave entitlements and offer bands now carries its salary structure), with the structure holding the component set (which earnings, which deductions), the formulas and amounts (or the amount SLOTS the assignment fills — the structure defining housing as 25% of basic while the assignment states the person's basic), and the effective machinery (structures versioned by date — the review that changes a structure creates the new version from its effective date, the old preserved: module 6 consumes this, and the frozen-history conviction of five tracks lands in payroll as the rule that a past month's structure is as sealed as its ledger).

The design conversation. Structures designed WITH the owner and accountant, from three inputs: the GRADE architecture (HR 1's bands — the structure count should roughly equal the grade count: the eleven-person firm with three grades runs three structures, and Chapter 9 will convict the 27-structures-for-27-people anti-pattern as the spreadsheet payroll wearing a system), the COMPONENT conventions (Chapter 3's split decisions, made once here — the basic share, the base flags, with the professionals' input on their consequences), and the MARKET position (HR 2's labour-market conversation, now with its machinery: the band's range lives in the structure's assignment rules — the grade 2 structure serving basics from X to Y, placements within it governed by the offer and review disciplines). The design output is small and load-bearing: a page per structure, signed, dated — the compensation constitution, beside the settings walks of every track.

Amendments as events. The structure's change discipline, in the academy's settled grammar: structure changes are EVENTS (the annual review's new version — module 6; the statutory change that moves a formula — module 2's reform landscape landing here; the component added to a class), effective-DATED (computing forward from their date, never silently rewriting the past — the March that was computed stays computed: the attendance close's one-version law, now at the structure layer), ANNOUNCED (the pay change nobody explained is module 4's query storm pre-ordered), and made by the narrowest pen (Chapter 7). The anti-pattern buried here by name: the quiet mid-year tweak — the formula nudged in place, no version, no date, no announcement — which makes every payslip before and after the tweak inconsistent with one of them, and converts the next dispute from a lookup into an archaeology.

What the structure buys, summarised. The template's dividends, collected for the sales conversation every consultant will have: the new hire priced in minutes (the offer from the band, the assignment from the structure — HR 2's discipline now with its engine), the review executed in hours (the version that moves a class — module 6), the statutory change absorbed in one edit (the formula updated once, every person on the structure correct next run — module 2's reform resilience), and the audit answered by pointing (WHY is this person paid this? — the structure, the assignment, the dates: three documents, no recollections). The structure is to pay what the chart was to accounts — the language, designed once, spoken everywhere — and the next chapter connects it to the people who earn from it.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — The assignment: person meets structure
lessons.html:
The structure defines the class; the ASSIGNMENT connects the person — the effective-dated record that says which structure, from when, with which amounts. The joining chapter.

The assignment's anatomy. Per employee: the STRUCTURE assigned (from their grade — the alignment that should be automatic and is audited because it drifts), the BASE amounts the structure's slots require (the person's basic, from which the formulas cascade — the one number the offer actually negotiated, landing in the one place it belongs), and the EFFECTIVE DATE (from which this assignment computes — the field the whole run reads, and the field every event of module 6 and HR 7 writes: the increment's date, the promotion's date, the structure version's date). The assignment is a DOCUMENT (created by the events that own it — the joiner package's onboarding, the review's increment, the promotion's re-pricing — never a quiet edit), and its history is the person's pay story: the assignments in sequence, each with its authorising event, is the answer to every 'since when' dispute the function will ever host.

The offer link: HR 2's discipline lands. The joining of the two tracks, made explicit: the offer from the grade's band (HR 2's law) becomes the assignment at onboarding (the joiner package carrying the agreed basic and the start date — the boundary's cleanest crossing when the offer was structural, and its messiest when it wasn't: the improvised offer arrives at payroll as a number with no structure to live in, and the consultant meets the resulting per-person 'structures' in every cleanup engagement). The proration reality at the edges: the mid-month joiner's first pay computed by the firm's stated day-count convention (calendar days or working days — a POLICY, chosen once, applied evenly, printed in the policy page, because the proration argued per case is the fairness leak module 7 will meet again at exits), and the convention's mirror applying to every mid-month event (the increment effective mid-month, the leaver's final days — one convention, every edge).

The no-structure employee. The error state named and fenced: the active employee with no current assignment is a run-time failure waiting for month-end (the run either skips them — the missed salary — or someone types a number — the improvisation this track exists to end), and the fence is structural: the joiner checklist's assignment line (HR 2's day-one readiness including the pay machinery), the pre-run validation that lists the unassigned (module 3's run discipline), and the monthly read that should always be empty. Its sibling error, equally fenced: the DOUBLE assignment (overlapping effective ranges — two answers to one month's question), refused by validation and resolved by dating discipline.

Currency, precision & the small print. The layer's technical hygiene, briefly and completely: amounts in the payroll currency at the ledger's precision (the precision mismatch that manufactures kobo residue at the payroll journal is Accounts 8's conviction arriving home), rounding rules stated per the firm's convention (the net rounded where practice rounds it, the difference carried to its component, never dropped — the kobo that vanishes monthly across 27 people is small money and large sloppiness), and annualisation conventions explicit (the annual package quoted at twelve months of gross unless the firm's terms say otherwise — the thirteenth-month arrangement, where the firm offers one, being module 5's governed variable pay, not a quiet convention). Small print, written down — because payroll's disputes live in exactly these crevices, and the policy page that pre-answers them is the function's quietest time-saver.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The gross-to-net walk & the modeling discipline
lessons.html:
The chapter that makes the structure REAL: one worked example, gross to net, every stop narrated — and the modeling discipline that puts this walk at the offer desk, where it prevents the most common compensation dispute in the trade. The arithmetic chapter.

The worked example: ₦250,000 gross. A grade 2 employee on the case-study structure — basic ₦125,000 (50%), housing ₦62,500 (25%), transport ₦37,500 (15%), utility allowance ₦25,000 (10%) — walked to net: Step 1, the statutory base — the pension base per the convention (basic + housing + transport = ₦225,000), flagged in Chapter 3's machinery, summed by the formula, not by hand. Step 2, the employee statutory shares — the employee pension contribution at its statutory rate (8% of the base = ₦18,000 — module 2 holds the law's detail; this chapter holds the flow), and PAYE per the current regime's computation on the taxable income after allowable deductions (the pension contribution reducing the taxable base before the bands apply — the interaction the spreadsheet payroll most often gets wrong, and the reason module 2 is this track's deep module: for this walk, the computed PAYE lands, illustratively, near ₦14,000 monthly under the reformed regime's bands for this income — the EXACT figure is module 2's terrain and the configuration's output, never a memorised number). Step 3, net — gross ₦250,000 minus ₦18,000 pension minus ~₦14,000 PAYE = ≈ ₦218,000 to the account. Step 4, the employer's total cost — gross PLUS the employer pension share (10% of the base = ₦22,500) plus the levies module 2 details: the ₦250k hire costs the firm ₦272,500+ monthly — the third number, delivered to the owner with the walk.

The walk's teaching uses. The example is machinery, not decoration: it is the CONFIGURATION TEST (the consultant runs this exact walk against the configured structure at implementation — the computed slip matching the hand walk to the naira is the go-live gate for the payroll layer: Accounts 1's posting-map verification, payroll edition), the TRAINING artifact (the payroll seat that can narrate this walk can answer module 4's queries; the one that cannot is operating a black box), and the DISPUTE settler (the payslip challenged is walked, line by line, against the structure — the drill-down culture of six tracks, at the payslip).

The modeling discipline: net at the offer desk. The chapter's operational payoff: candidates think in net — the offer stated as gross to a candidate budgeting in take-home is the misunderstanding that surfaces at the first payday as a grievance wearing a calculator — and the discipline is the net PREVIEW at the offer stage: the offer conversation equipped with the modeled slip (this gross, on this structure, yields this net — the modeling run the system makes trivial and the spreadsheet made heroic), the acceptance informed (HR 2's offer discipline gaining its missing number), and the same modeling serving the REVIEW conversations (module 6 — the increment's net effect shown, because the ₦20k gross increase that yields ₦14k net is a conversation better had with the number on the table) and the owner's budget (the employer-cost model per planned hire — HR 2's multi-million-naira-decision framing, now with its calculator).

The annualisation note. The walk's yearly shadow, closing the chapter: the statutory computations are ANNUAL creatures computed monthly (module 2's mechanics — the PAYE bands are annual bands, the reliefs annual reliefs, the monthly computation an instalment of a yearly truth), which is why mid-year changes ripple (the increment that moves the annual projection adjusts the remaining months' instalments) and why the year-end true-up disciplines exist (module 2's terrain). For this module, the takeaway is the frame: every monthly slip is one-twelfth of an annual story the statutory layer is keeping — and the consultant who holds that frame configures and explains; the one who doesn't debugs mysteries every January.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Governing the pay masters
lessons.html:
The layer's governance: who may touch the structures, components, and assignments — the narrowest pen in the firm — and the disciplines that keep the compensation constitution from eroding one favour at a time. The governance chapter.

The narrowest pen. The edit rights, tiered to the stakes: COMPONENTS and their flags (the atoms whose mis-flag mis-computes everyone — edited by the configure authority alone, with the accountant's sign-off on statutory flags: module 8 will seat this in the four-authorities pattern, but the rule lands now), STRUCTURES and their versions (the class-level truth — the same door, changed only by the events module 6 and module 2 define), and ASSIGNMENTS (the person-level connection — written by their owning events through the standing flows: the joiner package, the increment, the promotion, the separation — with the DIRECT edit right held by almost no one, because the assignment edited outside an event is precisely the negotiated-from-memory pay this track's first law forbids). The tiering's logic is blast radius: the component wounds everyone, the structure wounds a class, the assignment wounds a person — and the pen narrows as the radius widens.

The quiet-edit refusal. The disease this governance exists to refuse, named in its native habitat: the owner's just adjust Tunde's basic this month — the request every payroll seat receives, monthly, forever — met not with a lecture but with the CHANNELS: the one-off payment belongs in module 5's additional-pay machinery (documented, approved, visible on the slip as what it is), the permanent change belongs in module 6's review or HR 7's movement events (effective-dated, authorised, joined), and the direct edit belongs nowhere — because the quiet adjustment is invisible to the review (module 6 prices a band the private deals have already left), inconsistent at dispute (the payslip that matches no structure defends no one), and contagious (the first quiet favour recruits the second — the HR track's evenness law, at the layer where unevenness is denominated in naira). The consultant's gift to the payroll seat is exactly this paragraph, laminated: the channels exist so that saying yes is always possible and saying yes QUIETLY never is.

The audit trail & the reconciliation habit. The layer's self-evidence: every structure version, component change, and assignment carrying its who-when-why (the versioning machinery plus the change log — the pay story readable end to end), the quarterly STRUCTURE-TO-REALITY read (every active employee's assignment against their grade — the drift audit: the grade 3 person on a grade 2 structure is either an error or an undocumented decision, and both need surfacing), and the component review before each statutory season (module 2's pre-season ritual — the flags re-confirmed against the current law with the adviser, because the reform that moved a base definition moves a flag, and the flag moves everyone).

The confidentiality overlay. The governance's custody dimension, previewed for module 4's full treatment: the pay masters sit in the SENSITIVE tier of the HR track's permission design — the structures arguably readable more widely (the published band is HR 2's transparency choice, made deliberately), the ASSIGNMENTS emphatically not (the person's actual pay visible to the payroll function, the approver chain, and the person — and no one else by default: the compensation leak is the trade's fastest culture poison, and module 4 will treat the whole custody discipline). For this chapter, the governance conclusion: the pay masters are the firm's most consequential small dataset — a few structures, a few dozen assignments — governed by the narrowest pens, changed only by events, evidenced by trail, and fenced by the tightest tier. Small data, maximal governance: the inverse of every other layer's scale, and exactly right.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's structures are born
lessons.html:
The pay machinery, installed where five tracks prepared its ground. Every chapter clocks in.

The design sessions (Ch. 2-4). The compensation constitution built in two sittings with the MD and the accountant: the component set defined ONCE — the classic trio plus one utility allowance, statutory flags set with the accountant's sign-off (the pension base flagged as basic+housing+transport; taxability confirmed per component), and the sprawl fence agreed (new components by policy only — the 'special duty allowance' one early negotiation had invented is retired into the utility component with its holder's consent and a documented step-up: the museum's first exhibit, closed). THREE structures for three grades — not twenty-seven for twenty-seven (the spreadsheet era's per-person tabs formally convicted at the whiteboard) — each a page: component shares, formula bases, the band's assignment range, signed and dated. The vocabulary lands in the same sitting: the MD sees the three numbers for a grade 2 hire — ₦250k gross, ≈₦218k net, ₦272.5k+ employer cost — and the budget conversation audibly changes (I have been budgeting gross for eleven years).

The load (Ch. 5). Twenty-seven assignments, effective-dated, each from its document: the existing contracts mapped to their grade structures (twenty-four land cleanly in-band), and the three exceptions surfaced honestly — two legacy arrangements above band (documented as red-circled personal-to-holder terms with the adviser's shape: honoured, dated, and closed to inheritance) and one BELOW band (a quiet historic unfairness the structure exposes in an afternoon — corrected at the next run, effective-dated, with the back-conversation the MD chooses to have: the structure's first justice, delivered by architecture). The no-structure read runs empty; the double-assignment validation catches one overlapping date from the load and the dating is fixed the same hour.

The walk as the gate (Ch. 6). The configuration test: the ₦250k walk run by hand on the whiteboard, then computed by the configured structure — the two slips matching to the naira on the second attempt (the first attempt catches a utility-allowance taxability flag set wrong: the mis-flag that would have mis-computed ten people monthly, found by the walk exactly as the chapter promised — the go-live gate doing its one job). The modeling discipline installs at the offer desk the same week: the next hire's offer conversation includes the modeled net slip, and the candidate's acceptance email says so (first offer I've received that told me my take-home — the employer-brand dividend HR 2 predicted, arriving through payroll).

The governance tested (Ch. 7). Month two delivers the inevitable: just add thirty to Tunde's pay this month — he sorted the generator. The channels answer: the one-off lands in the additional-pay machinery as a documented, approved, visible bonus line (module 5's machinery, previewed live — thirty seconds of process, the favour granted WITHOUT the quiet edit), and the payroll seat's note in the file is the chapter's thesis in the wild: said yes through the channel; the structure never moved. The quarterly drift read runs clean; the component review is calendared before the statutory season. The layer ends its first quarter with three structures, twenty-seven true assignments, a tested walk, one closed museum exhibit, one corrected unfairness, and a governance that has already survived its first favour — the foundation module 2's statutory depth will now compute upon.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the first law
lessons.html:
The pay-structure layer's scar tissue — the diseases every payroll cleanup begins with. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — the spreadsheet payroll. Symptom: the monthly workbook, one tab per person or one row per arrangement; formulas nobody dares touch; the computation that lives in one head and one file. Disease: pay without masters (Ch. 1-2) — every month a fresh improvisation on last month's copy. Fix: the migration engagement — components defined, structures built per grade, assignments loaded from documents, the walk as the gate — and the workbook retired to read-only history beside HR 1's staff spreadsheet.

Pattern 2 — negotiated-from-memory pay. Symptom: 'his arrangement is different'; amounts recalled, not recorded; the dispute settled by whoever remembers loudest. Disease: the founder's memory as the pay master (Ch. 2, 7). Fix: every arrangement surfaced into an assignment with its document, the exceptions red-circled honestly, and the memory retired — the structure answering 'since when and why' by pointing.

Pattern 3 — the per-person structure. Symptom: twenty-seven structures for twenty-seven people; every review twenty-seven edits; the 'structure' layer as the spreadsheet wearing a doctype. Disease: the template's point missed (Ch. 4) — class machinery used as person storage. Fix: structures per grade, amounts in assignments, the band's range doing the individual work — the structure count collapsing to the grade count.

Pattern 4 — the mis-flagged component. Symptom: PAYE persistently 'a bit off'; the pension base disputed at remittance; the year-end true-up that surprises. Disease: the flag set wrong at birth, computing wrong for everyone since (Ch. 3). Fix: flags set with the accountant at creation, the walk as the configuration gate, the pre-season component review — one flag, checked, versus twelve months of quiet error.

Pattern 5 — the quiet edit. Symptom: payslips matching no structure; the review pricing a band the private deals have left; the favour that recruited its successors. Disease: the pen too wide and the channels unknown (Ch. 7). Fix: the narrowest pen tiered by blast radius, the channels laminated (one-offs to additional pay, permanence to events), and the drift read quarterly — saying yes always possible, saying yes quietly never.

Pattern 6 — gross confusion. Symptom: the payday grievance in week four ('this is not what we agreed'); the owner's budget missing the employer layer; three numbers used interchangeably in every conversation. Disease: the vocabulary never taught (Ch. 2, 6). Fix: the three numbers in every offer and review conversation, the net preview at the offer desk, the employer-cost model in the owner's budget — one walk, three audiences, zero surprises.

The first law. The sixth track opens where five tracks' grammar demands: pay is computed from structure, not negotiated from memory — few components precisely flagged, structures per grade versioned by date, assignments written only by their owning events, the gross-to-net walk as the gate and the teacher, and every favour granted through a channel that leaves the structure standing. The structure is pay's single source of truth: consistent by design, computable by flags, explainable by pointing, and changeable by class. Seven modules stand on it — and module 2 now takes the walk's hardest steps at full depth: the statutory layer, where the state rides every payslip and the reformed law sets the bands.

statutory.title: Payroll 2 — Statutory Deductions & Nigerian Compliance
statutory.desc: The track's deep module: statutory money as custody, PAYE under the reformed regime with the exemption floor and rent relief, the annual computation walk, the pension's fiduciary stream and seven-working-day clock, NHF/NSITF/ITF, the six-step remittance ritual, annual obligations, and the compliance architecture that absorbs reform in one configuration change.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The state rides every payslip
lessons.html:
The Accounts track's fifth module taught the custody thesis for the trading taxes; this module is its payroll sibling, and the thesis transfers whole with one sharpening: the statutory deductions on a payslip are custody money — collected from the worker or levied on the employer, held in passing, owed onward on a calendar — and the pension share carries a weight even VAT never did: it is a person's retirement, held in the firm's hands for seven working days.

The statutory inventory. The streams that ride Nigerian payroll, catalogued for the module's map: PAYE — the employee's income tax, withheld by the employer as agent, remitted to the STATE of the employee's residence (Chapters 2-3 — the module's largest resident, reshaped by the reformed tax law); the pension contributions — the Contributory Pension Scheme's two shares (the employee's, deducted; the employer's, added) into the employee's own Retirement Savings Account (Chapter 4 — the fiduciary stream); NHF — the National Housing Fund's employee contribution where in scope (Chapter 5); and the employer levies — NSITF's employee compensation contribution and ITF's training levy where the firm is in scope (Chapter 5 — the streams the worker never sees but the employer owes). Each stream has its base, its rate, its collector, its calendar, and its evidence — and the module walks each at consultant altitude.

The employee/employer split. The structural distinction every conversation needs: EMPLOYEE deductions (PAYE, the pension employee share, NHF) reduce net — they are the worker's money, withheld in trust; EMPLOYER contributions (the pension employer share, NSITF, ITF) sit ABOVE gross — they are the firm's own cost, the third number of module 1's vocabulary made itemised. The conflation of the two is the trade's standing confusion (the owner who thinks the 8% pension is the firm's cost; the worker who thinks NSITF came from their pay), and the consultant's untangling of it — one table, two columns — is frequently the first trust-building deliverable of a payroll engagement.

The adviser boundary, restated for this terrain. The grammar of two prior tracks, verbatim and load-bearing: the figures this module teaches are ORIENTATION — the shape of the regime, the conventional rates, the calendars as commonly administered — not advice; Nigerian tax law has just been rebuilt (the reform Acts effective from the 2026 tax year, whose payroll provisions Chapter 2 orients), states administer PAYE with local variation, scope thresholds move, and the ADVISER and the accountant own the firm's current reading, confirmed at the pre-season review (Chapter 8) and recorded on the policy page, dated. The consultant's identity sentence, payroll edition: I build the machinery that computes what your professionals confirm — I do not set rates, read reforms, or sign returns. With the boundary bright, the depth begins.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — PAYE under the reformed regime
lessons.html:
The module's largest stream, in its new landscape: PAYE after the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 — the reform that rebuilt personal income taxation from the 2026 tax year. The regime chapter, at consultant altitude.

The reform's shape. What changed, oriented: the old regime's Consolidated Relief Allowance is GONE — replaced by a new architecture: an exemption floor (annual taxable incomes up to ₦800,000 attract zero tax — the reform's headline mercy for low earners, which for a trading firm's junior roles can mean whole grades paying no PAYE at all), a rent relief (a deduction of 20% of annual rent paid, capped at ₦500,000 — claimed on the employee's declared rent, which makes the rent DECLARATION a new payroll input the system must capture and file: Chapter 8's architecture), and a new band structure above the floor (progressive rates stepping up through the annual income bands the Act sets, reaching the top marginal rate at the highest incomes — the bands' exact edges are the configuration's numbers, confirmed from the Act's schedule by the adviser, never recited from memory: the consultant knows the SHAPE — a zero band, then rising steps — and configures the current edges). The allowable deductions survive the reform: the pension contribution, NHF where paid — each reducing taxable income BEFORE the bands apply (module 1's walk already used this; Chapter 3 formalises it).

State collection. PAYE's administrative geography, unchanged in principle: the tax belongs to the STATE of the employee's residence — remitted to that state's revenue service (LIRS for Lagos residents, the respective SIRS elsewhere), which gives the multi-state firm a SPLIT remittance reality (the Ibadan branch's residents to Oyo's service, the Lagos staff to LIRS — the HR track's address data earning a tax consequence, and the employee's declared residence a governed field: Chapter 8's register carries it). The registration layer: the employer registered with each relevant state service, the employer's reference numbers on file, and the filing channels per state (the e-filing platforms where states run them) — the multi-state onboarding checklist the consultant builds once per client.

The transition posture. The consultant's stance in a reform's early years, taught as craft: configurations carry the CURRENT law with the OLD regime's logic retired but documented (the parallel-run discipline at changeover — the reformed computation run beside the old for one cycle's comparison, differences explained per person before the first live month: the walk of module 1, at regime scale), the workforce COMMUNICATED (the reform that changes nets without explanation is module 4's query storm at its worst — the net that ROSE for junior staff under the exemption floor is good news worth announcing; the senior whose relief architecture changed deserves the walk), and the adviser's confirmation dated on the policy page — because 'the new law says' is the adviser's sentence, and the consultant's contribution is a system that changes regimes by changing formulas, not by changing spreadsheets (the reform-resilience argument module 1 sold, now cashed at the largest possible scale: the trade's spreadsheet payrolls are still mis-computing the old regime; the structured firm changed one configuration).

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The PAYE computation walk
lessons.html:
The mechanics, end to end — the annual creature computed monthly, walked once slowly so the consultant can narrate it forever. The computation chapter.

The annual frame. PAYE is computed on ANNUAL taxable income against ANNUAL bands; the monthly deduction is an instalment of that yearly truth — so the computation ANNUALISES first: the monthly figures projected to the year (or the year-to-date actuals plus projection, per the configured method), the annual tax computed, and the month's share derived. The frame explains every mystery the spreadsheet era manufactured: why a mid-year increment changes the monthly tax by more than intuition suggests (the higher months re-project the year), why a bonus month spikes the deduction (module 5's variable pay entering the annual projection), and why December sometimes adjusts (the true-up — Chapter 7).

The walk, continuing module 1's case. The ₦250,000-gross grade 2 employee, now at full statutory depth — annualised: gross ₦3,000,000. Step 1, allowable deductions: the pension employee share (8% of the ₦2.7m annual base = ₦216,000) — deducted from gross income before tax; NHF where the employee is in scope (2.5% of annual basic = ₦37,500 in this case, if applicable — assume applicable for the walk). Step 2, rent relief: the employee's declared annual rent, say ₦600,000 — relief at 20% = ₦120,000 (inside the ₦500,000 cap). Step 3, taxable income: ₦3,000,000 − ₦216,000 − ₦37,500 − ₦120,000 = ₦2,626,500. Step 4, the bands: the first ₦800,000 at zero; the remainder walked up the Act's progressive steps — the configured schedule computing the annual tax (illustratively landing in the mid-₦200,000s annually for this income under the reformed bands — the precise figure is the configuration's output against the Act's schedule, which is the point: the consultant TRUSTS the configured bands they verified at Chapter 8's review, and never a remembered number). Step 5, the instalment: the annual tax ÷ 12 ≈ the monthly PAYE — the ~₦14,000-per-month figure module 1's walk previewed, now with its provenance shown.

The edges the walk must handle. The cases every configuration meets in year one: the MID-YEAR JOINER (taxed on this employment's annualised income per the configured convention, with the prior-employment declaration where the practice requires it — the adviser's shape), the MID-YEAR INCREMENT (the projection updated from its effective date — the remaining instalments absorbing the change), the LOW EARNER (the junior whose annual taxable income sits under the ₦800,000 floor computes to ZERO PAYE — the configuration must produce a clean zero, not a small wrong number, and the payslip must show the zero honestly), the VARIABLE MONTH (module 5's bonus entering the projection in its month — the spike explained by the annual frame, and explainable to the worker BY the payroll seat because this chapter taught them the frame), and the MULTI-STATE person (taxed where resident, moved when residence moves — an effective-dated fact from the HR record, never a guess).

The narration discipline. The chapter's closing craft note: the walk above is the payroll seat's core literacy — narratable on a whiteboard in four minutes — and the consultant certifies the seat exactly as module 1 prescribed: the person who can walk gross to PAYE by hand can answer every net-pay query, test every configuration, and survive every inspection conversation; the one who cannot is operating the academy's least forgivable black box, because this box computes people's take-home and the state's money in one pass.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Pension: the fiduciary stream
lessons.html:
The stream with the heaviest moral weight and the tightest calendar: the Contributory Pension Scheme — a person's retirement, computed on the firm's payroll, held in the firm's hands, owed to the person's own account within days. The pension chapter.

The scheme's shape. The Contributory Pension Scheme (the Pension Reform Act's architecture, PenCom-regulated): every eligible employee holds a Retirement Savings Account (RSA) with a Pension Fund Administrator of THEIR OWN CHOICE — the PFA is the employee's decision, not the employer's (the HR record's PFA field, captured at onboarding per the joiner package, is a choice recorded, never assigned — and the employee's right to transfer their RSA between PFAs is theirs to exercise, with the record updated when they do). The contributions: the conventional minimum rates — 8% employee, 10% employer — computed on the conventional base (monthly emoluments: basic + housing + transport — module 1's flagged base, doing here the exact work its flags were designed for), with voluntary additional contributions possible where the employee elects them (a governed deduction with its document, per module 5's machinery).

The remittance clock. The scheme's defining discipline: contributions remitted to each employee's RSA (via the PFA's custodian) within seven working days of paying the salary — the tightest standing deadline in Nigerian payroll, and the one this module treats as sacred, because the unremitted pension is not late paperwork: it is a PERSON'S RETIREMENT sitting in the firm's account earning the firm's interest — the fiduciary breach that compounds (the missed month becomes the missed quarter becomes the multi-year hole discovered when an employee tries to access their RSA), attracts penalties with interest for the employee's lost returns, and — the reputational dimension the consultant states plainly — is the single statutory failure workers monitor personally (the RSA statement is the worker's own document; the firm whose remittances don't appear is caught not by an inspector but by its own staff, at scale, with receipts).

The mechanics. The remittance's working parts: the contribution SCHEDULE per run (each employee: RSA PIN, PFA, the two shares, the base — generated from the payroll run's register, uploaded through the remittance channels the PFAs and custodians operate), the payment against the schedule (the separations of Accounts 3 governing the money movement as always), the RECEIPTS and upload confirmations filed to the evidence layer (Chapter 6), and the reconciliation habit: the per-employee remittance register (Chapter 8) against the schedules — because the pension stream's errors are PER-PERSON errors (the wrong RSA PIN sends a person's money into limbo; the stale PFA after a transfer bounces the upload), and the register that reconciles per person is the difference between a clean scheme and a drawer of unmatched receipts.

The employer's onboarding duties. The checklist per new hire: the RSA confirmed or opened (the new worker without an RSA guided to choose a PFA and open one — the employer's facilitation duty), the PIN captured and VERIFIED (the digit-perfect field — module 1's masters-not-messages discipline applying to the number that routes a retirement), and the group insurance layer the Act couples to the scheme (the employer's life insurance obligation for employees — the policy the adviser confirms and the firm maintains, noted here because inspections ask for it beside the pension evidence). The chapter's one-line law, for the wall above the payroll desk: the pension is not a deduction; it is a delivery — seven working days, every person, every month, evidenced.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — The smaller statutory layer: NHF, NSITF & ITF
lessons.html:
The streams beyond the big two — smaller in naira, identical in discipline, and the ones most often discovered unpaid at diligence. The levies chapter.

NHF — the National Housing Fund. The employee contribution to the federal housing scheme: 2.5% of monthly basic (basic alone — a different base from the pension's trio, which is exactly why module 1's per-component flags exist), deducted from employees in scope (the scope rules — income thresholds and the voluntary dimensions the reform era has adjusted — are the adviser's confirmation; the consultant's posture is the configured flag per employee, set from the confirmed reading, reviewed at the pre-season), remitted to the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria on the monthly calendar, evidenced, and reflected on the employee's NHF record (the contribution is the employee's own — their path to the fund's mortgage products — which gives NHF the pension's personal character in miniature: the worker's money, trackable by the worker).

NSITF — the employee compensation stream. The EMPLOYER'S levy (the worker never sees it): 1% of monthly payroll to the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund under the Employee Compensation Scheme — the insurance pool that compensates workplace injury, disability, and death (the scheme the Employee Compensation Act built), remitted monthly, evidenced by the ECS receipts, and CLAIMABLE against: the workplace injury the HR track's incident processes document is the event this levy insured, and the firm that pays NSITF but never files its certificate of compliance or knows the claims process has bought insurance it cannot use — the consultant's checklist adds the compliance certificate to the annual evidence file, because contracts and bids increasingly ask for it.

ITF — the training levy. The employer's contribution to the Industrial Training Fund: 1% of annual payroll for employers in scope (the scope thresholds — employee count and turnover tests — are the adviser's terrain and have moved with reform; the eligible small firm should confirm rather than assume either way), paid on the annual calendar, evidenced — and carrying the reimbursement dimension worth teaching: employers who TRAIN can claim partial refunds of the levy against approved training (the HR track's module 6 machinery — the curricula, the event records, the certificates — being exactly the evidence an ITF reimbursement claim runs on: the academy's training layer paying an unexpected statutory dividend, and the consultant who connects the two files has given the client money back).

The scope map & the levy calendar. The chapter's consolidating artifacts: the SCOPE MAP (per stream, per the adviser's confirmed reading: who is in — which employees for NHF, whether the firm for ITF — dated, reviewed annually, because scope answered by assumption is the diligence finding waiting to happen), and the LEVY CALENDAR (every stream's remittance date on one page — PAYE's monthly state deadline, pension's seven working days, NHF's monthly, NSITF's monthly, ITF's annual — the compliance calendar of Accounts 5 gaining its payroll column, and Chapter 6 wiring it into the ritual). The smaller streams' collective lesson: none is large; all are findable; and the firm that runs them on the same ritual as the big two spends minutes monthly, while the firm that ignores them until diligence spends the difference in penalties, back-payments, and the deal-room's raised eyebrow.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Remittance mechanics: the custody ritual
lessons.html:
Accounts 5 built the six-step ritual for the trading taxes; this chapter adapts it to the payroll streams — same shape, tighter clocks, more collectors. The ritual chapter.

The six steps, payroll edition. Per stream, per cycle: 1 — COMPUTE from the run (the statutory register per stream generated by the payroll run itself — Chapter 8's architecture: the schedules are outputs, never separate spreadsheets, because the separately-maintained schedule is the version-drift disease at the custody layer); 2 — RESERVE (the custody discipline of Accounts 5 verbatim: the statutory money moved to or marked in the custody position at the run, not discovered at the deadline — the reserve that makes the remittance a transfer instead of a scramble, and the conviction restated in payroll's sharper terms: the firm 'borrowing' the PAYE and pension for three weeks of cashflow is borrowing from its workers and the state at the most expensive interest in Nigeria — penalty rates plus fiduciary breach plus the trust of everyone whose payslip said the money was deducted); 3 — FILE the returns and schedules per collector's channel (the state e-filings, the pension uploads); 4 — REMIT against the filings (the payment separations governing); 5 — EVIDENCE (the receipts, acknowledgments, and upload confirmations into the stream's dated folder — the evidence file that answers inspections in minutes); 6 — ZERO (the custody account per stream returning to zero after remittance — Accounts 5's zeroing invariant, now multiplied across the payroll streams: the PAYE custody, the pension custody, each read post-remittance, each explainable or zero).

The custody accounts. The ledger's payroll-statutory architecture (Accounts 2's payroll journal, now itemised): the run's journal crediting each statutory stream's liability account (the PAYE withheld, the pension shares, NHF, the levies accrued), the remittances debiting them to zero, and the month-end read (the accounts at their explainable levels — the post-remittance zero, or the current month's accrual awaiting its date, and NOTHING older: the aged statutory balance is the unremitted month wearing an account balance, and the Accounts track's trial-balance scan will catch it, which is the two tracks' machinery cross-checking exactly as designed).

The penalty economics, quantified in kind. The owner conversation, equipped as Accounts 5 equipped it: each stream carries penalties for late or absent remittance (the percentages and interest per stream are the adviser's current numbers), and the structural point survives every rate change: penalties are computed on money the firm ALREADY COLLECTED — the fine is for failing to forward, which makes every naira of payroll-statutory penalty a pure loss purchased by disorganisation — plus the pension stream's interest-for-lost-returns dimension, plus the compliance certificates (the tax clearance, the pension clearance, the NSITF certificate) that bids and contracts demand and arrears block: the unremitted month costs money, and it also costs the next contract. The reserve discipline is the entire cure, and it costs a ledger entry.

The calendar, owned. The chapter's closing wiring: every stream's dates on the levy calendar (Chapter 5), the calendar's lines OWNED (the named remitter, the named verifier — the two-names pattern at the custody desk), the seven-working-day pension clock tracked from each payment date (not month-end — the clock starts when salaries move), and the ritual's completion logged per stream per cycle. The firm running this chapter spends a predictable hour monthly; the firm that doesn't runs Chapter 10's patterns — and the consultant's install of this one page is, measured in penalties averted, frequently the highest-ROI hour of the whole engagement.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Annual obligations: the year-end layer
lessons.html:
The monthly ritual has an annual shadow: the returns, reconciliations, and true-ups that close each tax year. The January chapter — made boring by twelve clean months, exactly as Accounts 7 promised for the books.

The employer's annual return. The headline obligation: the annual PAYE return to each relevant state — the employer's declaration of every employee, their annual emoluments, and the tax deducted and remitted (the return conventionally due in January for the preceding year — the deadline per state, confirmed current by the adviser), assembled not composed: the per-employee statutory register (Chapter 8) IS the return's content, and the firm that kept the register files by export while the firm that didn't reconstructs a year from payslips in the trade's least loved week. The return's counterpart obligations ride the same season: the projection declarations where states require them (the coming year's estimated payroll), and the reconciliations the state's system runs (the return against the year's monthly remittances — the mismatch that surfaces here is the unremitted or mis-referenced month, found by the collector if the firm's own reads didn't find it first).

The employee-facing layer. The year-end's personal documents: the employee's evidence of tax deducted (the deduction certificates and payslip year-summaries the firm provides — the inputs to the employee's own Tax Clearance Certificate when they need one: the TCC that banks, embassies, and agencies request is issued by the state on the strength of the taxes the employer remitted in their name, which makes the firm's remittance discipline a PERSONAL service to every employee — the worker denied a TCC because their employer's remittances don't reconcile has been failed twice, and knows exactly by whom), and the rent-relief declarations refreshed for the new year (the reformed regime's annual input — Chapter 2's new field, re-declared and filed on the year's calendar).

The pension year-end. The fiduciary stream's annual reads: the per-employee remittance reconciliation (the year's schedules against the register — every person, every month, matched; the unmatched upload chased with the PFA while the trail is warm), the RSA statement conversation (employees encouraged to READ their annual RSA statements against their payslips — the transparency that costs nothing and catches everything, because twenty-seven personal auditors beat one annual review), and the group life policy's renewal on the calendar (Chapter 4's coupled obligation, renewed before it lapses rather than discovered lapsed at a claim).

The true-up. The annual frame's settlement (Chapter 3's projection meeting the year's actuals): the December computation reconciling each person's year — the actual annual income against the instalments deducted — with the final month absorbing the difference within the configured method's tolerances (the small December adjustment is the annual creature closing its books; the LARGE December swing is a configuration or data problem that the monthly walk should have caught earlier — the true-up's size is itself a health read on the whole year's computation). The chapter's closing economics, in the academy's oldest cadence: the annual season for a firm that ran Chapters 3-6 monthly is an export, a reconciliation, and a filing — days, not weeks; the season for the firm that didn't is the January scramble Chapter 10 convicts — and the difference was never January; it was the other eleven months.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — The compliance architecture: configured, registered, resilient
lessons.html:
The chapter where the module's law becomes configuration: the statutory layer wired into the system so that computation, registers, calendars, and reform-resilience are architecture, not effort. The machinery chapter.

The formulas, from the flags. Module 1's design cashing at full depth: each statutory component a FORMULA on its flagged base (the pension shares on the flagged trio; NHF on basic; PAYE as the configured annual computation — the bands, the exemption floor, the reliefs, the allowable-deduction interactions all in the tax configuration the system computes per person per run), with the configuration's numbers sourced from the adviser-confirmed policy page and TESTED by the walk (Chapter 3's hand computation against the system's slip — per structure, at install and at every change: the go-live gate of module 1, now guarding the state's money too). The configuration's virtue restated as the sales argument it is: the reform that moves a band, a rate, or a relief is ONE configuration change, effective-dated, applied evenly — the structured firm absorbs tax reform in an afternoon; the spreadsheet firm mis-computes for months.

The registers. The layer's memory, per stream, per person: the statutory register — each employee's monthly record per stream (the base, the computation, the deduction, the remittance reference) accumulating into the year — which IS the annual return (Chapter 7), IS the pension reconciliation, IS the inspection answer, and IS the employee's query answer (module 4's transparency reaching the statutory lines: the worker who asks 'where did my tax go' is shown their register row and the remittance receipt — the question answered by pointing, in the academy's oldest gesture). The register's inputs are the run's outputs by construction (no separately-maintained schedules — the version-drift fence), and its governed fields include the identity layer the streams route on: the Tax Identification Number, the RSA PIN, the declared residence state, the NHF number, the rent declaration — each captured at onboarding (the joiner package's statutory section), verified digit-perfect, and maintained as the effective-dated facts they are.

The calendar, wired. The levy calendar (Chapters 5-6) living in the system: the remittance tasks generated per cycle with their owners and clocks (the pension's seven-working-day timer started by the salary payment date — the automation that watches the module's tightest deadline so no human has to remember it), the evidence uploads attached to the completed tasks (the ritual's step 5 leaving its trail where the inspection will look), and the completion log the compliance certificate season reads.

The pre-season review. The annual architecture ritual, scheduled before each tax year: the adviser session (the year's rates, bands, thresholds, and scope readings confirmed — the reform landscape read by its owner), the configuration updated effective the year's start (versioned, dated — module 1's amendment discipline at the statutory layer), the component flags re-verified (the mis-flag hunt of module 1's review, now with the adviser in the room), the scope map refreshed (Chapter 5), the rent declarations collected for the new year (Chapter 2's input), and the walk re-run against the updated configuration (the gate, annually). One meeting, one afternoon of configuration, one tested walk — and the firm enters the year computing the current law evenly for everyone, which is the entire promise of this chapter's title: compliance as ARCHITECTURE — configured once, registered continuously, resilient by design.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Case study: HealthTrade's statutory year
lessons.html:
The statutory layer, installed on module 1's structures and run through a full year. Every chapter clocks in.

The install & the regularisation (Ch. 1, 6). The registration audit opens the engagement: PAYE registrations verified with the two relevant states (Lagos and Oyo — the multi-state map drawn from the HR records' residences), the pension employer codes confirmed, NSITF current — and ITF discovered UNREGISTERED despite the firm being in scope since crossing the threshold two years prior: the finding handled by the book — quantified, taken to the ADVISER, and regularised through the proper channel (the back-levy computed, the position negotiated by the professional who owns it, the registration completed) — the consultant's boundary held exactly as three tracks taught (found and quantified by the machinery; resolved by the adviser), and the diligence landmine defused before it could meet a deal room.

The configuration & the parallel run (Ch. 2-3, 8). The reformed regime configured from the adviser session: the exemption floor, the bands from the Act's schedule, rent relief with its declaration flow (twenty-seven declarations collected in a week through self-service — the new input operationalised), pension and NHF formulas on their flagged bases. The parallel run compares the reformed computation against the old for one cycle: the junior grades' PAYE drops to ZERO under the ₦800,000 floor (nine people — the announcement at the branch meetings lands the reform as the good news it is, pre-empting the confusion), the senior computations walked and explained individually. The walk gates go-live: the ₦250k case computed by hand and by system — matching to the naira, first attempt this time (module 1's flag lesson having been learned).

The ritual, monthly (Ch. 4-6). The six steps run per stream from month one: the schedules generated from the run, the reserve moved at computation (the MD's cashflow instinct meets the custody thesis in one sentence — that money was never ours — and the reserve discipline holds), the pension's seven-working-day clock beaten every month (the automation's timer plus the named remitter — the tightest deadline made routine), evidence filed per stream per month, custody accounts zeroing on the trial balance (the Accounts track's scan confirming the payroll track's discipline — the two certifications cross-checking in production). One catch proves the register: month five's pension upload bounces ONE person — a stale PFA after an employee's RSA transfer (the record updated within the week, the contribution re-routed, the person shown their register row and the corrected receipt: the per-person reconciliation catching the per-person error, exactly as Chapter 4 designed).

The annual season (Ch. 7). January arrives boring: the annual returns to both states exported from the register and filed inside the deadline (the Oyo filing's first year taking an afternoon; the reconstruction it replaced had taken the accountant most of a prior February), the deduction summaries issued to all staff (two employees request TCC support that quarter — both clean, because the remittances reconcile), the pension year-reconciliation matching every person every month, the RSA-statement conversation held at the branch meetings (one employee's statement query traces to a PRE-system employer's gap, documented for their own pursuit — the register proving the firm's own year whole), rent declarations refreshed, the true-up landing small across the workforce (the annual frame's health read: the year computed clean). The MD's year-note closes the case: the state rides every payslip — and for the first time, it rides in its own seat, on time, with receipts.

lessons.title: Chapter 10 — Common mistakes & the second law
lessons.html:
The statutory layer's scar tissue — the patterns behind most payroll penalties in the trade. Symptom → disease → fix.

Pattern 1 — statutory money as cashflow. Symptom: the PAYE and pension 'borrowed' for stock; remittances timed to the bank balance; the deadline met in good months and missed in tight ones. Disease: custody treated as float (Ch. 1, 6) — borrowing from workers and the state at Nigeria's most expensive interest. Fix: the reserve at the run, the custody accounts zeroing, the calendar owned — the money that was never the firm's, never touched.

Pattern 2 — the unremitted pension. Symptom: deductions on every payslip; nothing landing in RSAs; the multi-year hole discovered by an employee's statement. Disease: the fiduciary stream treated as the softest deadline when it is the hardest (Ch. 4). Fix: the seven-working-day clock automated from the payment date, the per-person register reconciled, the RSA-statement transparency recruited — twenty-seven personal auditors, invited.

Pattern 3 — the flat-rate guess. Symptom: PAYE at a uniform percentage 'to keep it simple'; the exemption floor ignored; juniors over-taxed and seniors under-taxed, both wrongly. Disease: the computation replaced by folklore (Ch. 2-3) — and the reform era makes yesterday's folklore doubly wrong. Fix: the configured annual computation on the current bands, the walk as the gate, the parallel run at every regime change — and the workforce told, because the corrected nets are conversations either way.

Pattern 4 — the January scramble. Symptom: the annual return reconstructed from payslips; the reconciliation mismatches surfacing at the state's system; February lost to archaeology. Disease: no register — the year never accumulated (Ch. 7-8). Fix: the statutory register as the run's output, the annual return as an export — January boring because the other eleven months were structured.

Pattern 5 — the scope-by-assumption levy. Symptom: NHF deducted from everyone or no one by habit; ITF unregistered 'because we're small' past the threshold; NSITF paid but the certificate never collected. Disease: scope answered by assumption instead of the adviser's reading (Ch. 5). Fix: the scope map, adviser-confirmed and dated, reviewed annually — and the compliance certificates filed where the bids will ask for them.

Pattern 6 — the digit-drift identity. Symptom: pension uploads bouncing; a person's contributions in limbo; tax remitted against a wrong or absent TIN; the residence state guessed. Disease: the identity fields ungoverned (Ch. 8) — the numbers that route money treated as free text. Fix: the statutory identity section of the joiner package, digit-perfect verification, effective-dated maintenance — masters-not-messages, applied to the fields that carry a retirement.

The second law. Module 1 made pay a structure; this module seats the state in it: statutory money is custody — the payslip's second passenger: computed from configured law on flagged bases, reserved at the run, remitted on each stream's clock with the pension's seven days held sacred, evidenced per stream, zeroed per cycle, registered per person, and reconciled until every worker's money reached every worker's account. The firm that runs this law spends an hour a month and files January by export; the firm that doesn't funds the state's penalty book and its workers' distrust from the same account. Module 3 now assembles everything — the structures, the statutory layer, the HR packages — into the function's heartbeat: the payroll run itself.
